events.continuity_hook: Continues the Denver conference lodging decision while flights remain on hold.
events.interaction_goal: Select a refundable lodging hold and list the room and amenity details Kara should confirm before the cancellation deadline.
events.scenario_brief: The association posts the Denver room-block cutoff and only a handful of refundable rooms remain. The most convenient conference hotel has uneven recent ratings and unclear mini-fridge availability, while a nearby 4.3-rated hotel is outside the block but has a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, and fitness room, with no hot tub listed. Kara still does not have the final breakout time, so the unresolved choice is whether to hold the official room for convenience or reserve the stronger nearby option before rates move.

events.continuity_hook: Moves Denver from lodging hold to the main booking decision now that the presentation schedule is set.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Denver flight and hotel booking, choose the least tiring return plan, and secure a window seat if one is available.
events.scenario_brief: Kara's Friday breakout is confirmed for late morning, and the Saturday conference schedule now ends by 4:00 p.m. This makes a Thursday arrival workable and opens a Sunday afternoon return to Tampa, but the best airfare involves one connection and the window-seat map is already thin. The previously favored nearby hotel still has the queen room with coffee maker and mini-fridge, but the rate is no longer fully flexible after midnight.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new seminar-weekend plan while Denver is booked but still weeks away.
events.interaction_goal: Build an initial flight-and-hotel shortlist and identify the host questions needed before Kara commits.
events.scenario_brief: A children's therapy program in St. Louis asks Kara to teach a late-July pediatric balance course with Friday afternoon setup, a full Saturday class, and a possible Sunday lab. She can leave Tampa only after a Thursday morning teaching block, needs a hotel within a practical commute of the medical campus, and wants a return that will not make Monday clinic prep miserable. The host has not yet confirmed whether Sunday's lab ends at lunch or midafternoon.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the St. Louis plan after the lab end time and host hotel list make the trade-offs clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Rank the hotel choices by commute reliability and room basics, then pair them with safe Sunday return windows.
events.scenario_brief: The St. Louis host confirms the Sunday lab will run until 2:30 p.m. and sends a preferred hotel list. The closest property is attached to a clinic garage but has weaker guest feedback and only lists double beds; a better-rated suite hotel 12 minutes out has a queen room, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, pool, and fitness room, but no hot tub and a less predictable drive for Friday setup. Return flights now need to leave late enough for teardown and airport transfer.

events.continuity_hook: Reopens Denver only because airline and hotel notices arrived shortly before travel.
events.interaction_goal: Check whether the updated return and hotel conditions are still workable, and decide whether to keep the current reservations.
events.scenario_brief: A week before Denver departure, the airline moves Kara's Sunday return 70 minutes earlier and the conference app shifts badge pickup to a different convention-center entrance. Her hotel says the pool will be closed for resurfacing, though the fitness room remains open and the room still has the coffee maker and mini-fridge. She needs to decide whether the earlier return still leaves enough time after an optional Sunday educator breakfast and whether the closed pool is worth changing hotels this late.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a personal active-weekend episode after the Denver conference travel is mostly behind her.
events.interaction_goal: Compare drive-versus-fly logistics and choose the hotel base that best fits the trail weekend and recovery time.
events.scenario_brief: After Denver, Kara and her partner start planning a late-summer Blue Ridge weekend around a Saturday trail event near Asheville and a recovery day on Sunday. They can leave Tampa Friday morning or early afternoon and return Monday, and the decision is not just price: flying into a larger airport means a longer rental-car drive, while driving the whole way may cost them a full day each direction. Hotel options split between a downtown inn with strong ratings but limited recovery facilities and a mountain-area lodge with pool, hot tub, and fitness access but less certainty on room coffee and refrigerator.
